_readme: One object per target market. Drives /countries/<slug>/ pages, which list the
bookmakers whose `countries` array contains this slug.
IMPORTANT: gambling law changes often and varies by region. Verify every legal
line with a current source (and ideally a lawyer) before publishing — this is
YMYL content and Google holds it to a higher bar. `verify: true` marks entries

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.legal_summary: Online sports betting is legal and tightly regulated. Operators serving UK players must hold a UKGC licence, which brings strict rules on advertising, affordability checks and player protection.
key_facts: Credit cards cannot be used for gambling (banned since April 2020)
All licensed operators must participate in GAMSTOP self-exclusion
Winnings are not taxed for the player

countries.name: Germany
countries.legal_summary: Regulated nationally under the 2021 State Treaty on Gambling. Licensed operators may offer sports betting, but the framework is noticeably stricter than in most of Europe.
key_facts: Cross-operator monthly deposit limit applies by default
Live betting is restricted to a limited set of markets
A betting turnover tax applies and some operators pass it to the customer

countries.name: India
countries.regulator: Regulated at state level — no single national licence
countries.legal_summary: Rules differ by state: several states permit online betting while others prohibit it outright. Many international operators accept Indian players, so check the law where you live before signing up.
key_facts: Rules vary significantly between states
UPI and local wallets are the most common deposit methods
Winnings are subject to tax deducted at source

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.regulator: National Lottery Regulatory Commission and state boards
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal and popular, with both locally licensed operators and international sites serving the market. Football, and the Premier League in particular, dominates betting volume.
key_facts: Mobile-first market — most bets are placed on phones
Bank transfer and mobile money are the leading payment methods
Data-light apps matter because of connection costs

countries.name: Kenya
key_facts: One of Africa's highest betting participation rates — mobile-first market
M-Pesa dominates deposits and withdrawals
Stakes and winnings are taxed; rates change frequently, so check current rules
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal and licensed by the BCLB. Operators need a local licence, and betting taxes (on stakes and winnings) are a recurring political topic — rates change often.

countries.name: Ghana
key_facts: Licensed operators are listed publicly by the Gaming Commission
Mobile money is the default payment rail
A withholding tax applies to winnings — check the current rate
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal and regulated by the Gaming Commission of Ghana. Only licensed operators may take bets, and a withholding tax on winnings has applied since 2023.

countries.name: Tanzania
key_facts: Betting is licensed and openly regulated — the Gaming Board publishes operator lists
Mobile money covers nearly all deposits
Gaming tax applies to winnings
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal under the Gaming Act, overseen by the Gaming Board of Tanzania. Licensed local operators dominate, and winnings are subject to gaming tax.

countries.name: Uganda
key_facts: Operators must hold an LGRB licence
Mobile money is the leading payment method
A tax on winnings applies — check the current rate before withdrawing
countries.legal_summary: Betting is legal and regulated by the Lotteries and Gaming Regulatory Board. Licensing is enforced and a withholding tax applies to winnings.

countries.name: South Africa
key_facts: Online sports betting is legal via provincially licensed bookmakers
Online casino games are NOT legal — only licensed betting
Recreational winnings are generally not taxed
countries.legal_summary: Online sports betting is legal when the bookmaker holds a provincial licence (e.g. Western Cape, Mpumalanga). Online casino gaming remains prohibited — a key distinction unique to South Africa.

countries.name: Peru
key_facts: Online betting has been formally regulated since 2024
Licensed operators are registered with MINCETUR
Local wallets Yape and Plin are the fastest deposit routes
countries.legal_summary: Peru regulated online sports betting in 2024 under MINCETUR. Licensed operators may advertise and take bets legally — one of Latin America's newest regulated markets.

countries.name: Chile
countries.regulator: No dedicated online regulator yet (framework pending)
key_facts: Online betting is a grey market — a regulation bill is pending in Congress
Land-based casinos are regulated separately (SCJ)
Offshore sites are widely used in the meantime
countries.legal_summary: Chile has no dedicated online betting framework yet: offshore operators serve the market while a regulation bill moves through Congress. Check the current status before signing up.

countries.name: Colombia
key_facts: First Latin American country to regulate online betting (2016)
Licensed sites operate on .co domains under Coljuegos
Winnings above a threshold are taxed
countries.legal_summary: Online betting is fully legal and regulated by Coljuegos — Latin America's pioneer market. Only Coljuegos-licensed operators may legally serve Colombian players.

countries.name: Senegal
key_facts: Betting is permitted under state oversight via LONASE
Mobile money (Orange Money, Wave) dominates payments
Football betting drives the vast majority of volume
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is permitted in Senegal under the oversight of the state lottery LONASE, with both local and international operators serving the market.

countries.name: Côte d'Ivoire
key_facts: Betting operates under the state lottery LONACI's oversight
Mobile money is the default deposit method
One of francophone Africa's largest betting markets
countries.legal_summary: Betting is permitted in Côte d'Ivoire under LONACI oversight. The market is mobile-first and one of the largest in francophone West Africa.

countries.name: Brazil
key_facts: Fixed-odds betting is federally licensed since January 2025
Licensed operators must use .bet.br domains
PIX instant payments dominate deposits and withdrawals
countries.legal_summary: Brazil's regulated market went live in January 2025 under the Ministry of Finance's betting secretariat (SPA). Only licensed operators on .bet.br domains may legally serve Brazilian players.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.regulator: SEGOB (Dirección General de Juegos y Sorteos)
key_facts: Online betting operates under SEGOB permits, often via land-based licence holders
OXXO cash vouchers remain a popular deposit route
A new gambling law has been debated for years — rules may change
countries.legal_summary: Betting is legal in Mexico under SEGOB permits issued via the Federal Gaming Law. Many online brands operate under agreements with land-based permit holders while a modernised law remains pending.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.regulator: Provincial regulators (LOTBA, IPLyC PBA and others)
key_facts: Regulation is province-by-province — Buenos Aires City and Province license online operators
Mercado Pago is the default payment rail
Currency volatility makes payout speed matter more than usual
countries.legal_summary: Online betting in Argentina is regulated at the provincial level: Buenos Aires City (LOTBA) and Buenos Aires Province license online operators, and other provinces run their own regimes. Check the rules for your province.

countries.name: Canada
key_facts: Single-event betting has been legal nationwide since 2021
Ontario runs a fully licensed open market (iGaming Ontario)
Recreational winnings are not taxed
countries.legal_summary: Canada legalised single-event sports betting in 2021. Ontario operates an open licensed market under AGCO/iGaming Ontario, while other provinces offer betting through provincial lottery platforms — with offshore sites in a grey area outside Ontario.

countries.name: Ireland
key_facts: The Gambling Regulation Act 2024 created a new dedicated regulator (GRAI)
Bookmakers historically licensed via the Revenue Commissioners
Winnings are not taxed for the punter
countries.legal_summary: Betting is fully legal in Ireland. Licensing is transitioning from the Revenue Commissioners to the new Gambling Regulatory Authority of Ireland under the Gambling Regulation Act 2024.

countries.name: Cameroon
key_facts: Betting is permitted with local licences and is hugely popular
Mobile money covers nearly all deposits
One of central Africa's largest betting markets
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is permitted in Cameroon under state licensing, with both local and international brands active. The market is mobile-first and football-driven.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.regulator: No dedicated regulator — taxation of online betting introduced, framework evolving
key_facts: Land-based casinos were banned by referendum in 2011; online betting is a grey area
A tax on online betting operators and players was introduced recently
The US dollar is the official currency — no conversion needed
countries.legal_summary: Ecuador has no dedicated online betting framework: offshore sites serve the market while the state has begun taxing online betting — a sign regulation is evolving. Check the current rules before signing up.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.regulator: Betting Control and Licensing (Ministry of Finance)
key_facts: Betting is legal and licensed under the Betting Control Act
Mobile money is the default payment rail
A fast-growing market with little SEO competition
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal in Zambia under the Betting Control Act, with licensed local operators and mobile-money payments dominating the market.

countries.name: Benin
key_facts: Betting operates under state oversight built around the national lottery
Mobile money is the default deposit and withdrawal rail
Rules have been reformed repeatedly — check the current position
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting in Benin operates under state oversight organised around the national lottery framework, with local and international operators serving a mobile-first market. The regime has been reorganised more than once in recent years, so confirm the current rules before signing up.

countries.name: Togo
key_facts: Betting sits under state oversight via the national lottery LONATO
Flooz and T-Money handle most deposits
Football, and European leagues in particular, drives the volume
countries.legal_summary: Betting in Togo falls under state oversight through the national lottery LONATO. The market is small but almost entirely mobile, with local wallets handling deposits and withdrawals.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
key_facts: The state lottery LONAB anchors the licensed framework
Orange Money and Moov Money dominate payments
Data costs make lightweight apps a real selection criterion
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting in Burkina Faso operates under state oversight centred on the national lottery LONAB, with international operators also serving the market. Payments run almost entirely through mobile money.

countries.name: Mali
key_facts: Betting operates under state oversight via the national lottery framework
Orange Money is the default payment rail
European football dominates betting interest
countries.legal_summary: Betting in Mali operates under state oversight organised around the national lottery, with international operators active alongside local ones. Mobile money handles effectively all deposits and payouts.

countries.name: Niger
key_facts: The national lottery LONANI anchors state oversight of betting
Airtel Money and Orange Money handle most transactions
A small, strongly mobile-first market
countries.legal_summary: Betting in Niger falls under state oversight through the national lottery LONANI. The market is small and mobile-first, with mobile money the practical way to fund an account.

countries.name: DR Congo
countries.regulator: Government licensing (Ministry of Finance / lottery authority)
key_facts: Operators need government authorisation to take bets legally
Mobile money (M-Pesa, Airtel Money, Orange Money) dominates
One of the largest betting populations in Central Africa
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is licensed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo through government authorisation, with several large operators active in a mobile-first market. Confirm an operator's current licence status before depositing.

countries.name: Angola
key_facts: Sports betting is licensed and supervised by the ISJ under the Ministry of Finance
Multicaixa Express dominates deposits and withdrawals
European football drives most betting volume
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal in Angola under licensing supervised by the Instituto de Supervisão de Jogos (ISJ). Licensed local operators and international brands both serve the market, with payments running through Multicaixa Express and bank rails.

countries.name: Mozambique
key_facts: Betting is licensed under Mozambique's gaming law, overseen by the state gaming inspectorate
M-Pesa and e-Mola mobile money handle most deposits
A gaming tax framework applies — check current rules before withdrawing
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal in Mozambique under the national gaming law, with licensing overseen by the state gaming inspectorate. Mobile money (M-Pesa, e-Mola) is the practical payment rail for most bettors.

countries.name: Ethiopia
key_facts: Sports betting is licensed by the National Lottery Administration — retail betting shops are a fixture of every Ethiopian city
telebirr and CBE Birr dominate deposits and withdrawals; M-Pesa arrived with Safaricom in 2023
Winnings from games of chance carry a 15% withholding tax — small amounts are exempt, thresholds change, check current rules
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal and licensed by the National Lottery Administration (NLA). Licensed operators run retail and online books in birr; offshore sites sit outside NLA supervision, so a payout dispute there has no local recourse.

countries.name: United States
countries.regulator: State gaming regulators (NJ DGE, PGCB, MGCB and peers)
key_facts: Legal sports betting is licensed state by state — roughly 38 states plus DC since the 2018 PASPA repeal
Odds are quoted American-style (+150 / −200); every book runs its own state-approved app
Offshore sites are illegal in most states and attorneys general send cease-and-desist orders — stick to state-licensed operators
countries.legal_summary: Sports betting is legal at the state level since the Supreme Court struck down PASPA in 2018. Each state licenses operators separately, so availability, taxes and even the minimum age differ across state lines; offshore books remain illegal in most states.

countries.name: Netherlands
key_facts: Online betting has been licensed under the KOA Act since October 2021
CRUKS — the national self-exclusion register — is mandatory across every licensed operator
Advertising rules are among Europe's strictest: untargeted gambling ads have been banned since 2023
countries.legal_summary: Fully regulated: online sports betting is legal with a Kansspelautoriteit licence under the KOA Act (2021). Unlicensed operators are actively fined, and the CRUKS self-exclusion register applies market-wide.

countries.name: Sweden
key_facts: Re-regulated in 2019: licensed private operators replaced the old monopoly
BankID verification is universal — registration and payouts are near-instant
Spelpaus.se self-exclusion covers every licensed site at once; bonuses are capped at one welcome offer per operator
countries.legal_summary: Legal and licensed by Spelinspektionen since the 2019 re-regulation. Licensed sites must connect to Spelpaus (national self-exclusion) and may offer only a single welcome bonus — a deliberate consumer-protection trade-off.

countries.name: Poland
key_facts: Only bookmakers licensed by the Ministry of Finance may operate; unlicensed domains go on the national block register
A 12% turnover tax on stakes is priced into Polish odds — factor it into any value calculation
BLIK dominates deposits and withdrawals at licensed books
countries.legal_summary: Legal but tightly controlled: sports betting requires a Ministry of Finance licence, unlicensed sites are DNS-blocked via the state register, and a 12% turnover tax on stakes shapes the odds licensed books can offer.

countries.name: Switzerland
key_facts: Sports betting is run by the Swisslos and Loterie Romande lottery societies under the 2019 Money Gaming Act
Unauthorised foreign betting sites are DNS-blocked by the authorities
Winnings from licensed Swiss games are tax-free up to CHF 1 million
countries.legal_summary: Legal within a controlled system: the 2019 Money Gaming Act reserves sports betting for the cantonal lottery societies (Swisslos and Loterie Romande) under Gespa supervision, and unauthorised foreign sites are DNS-blocked.
